usage: Usually used as a countable noun for a type of gemstone. It often appears after numbers or measure words, for example when talking about one stone or several stones.
Common in jewellery and luxury contexts. You’ll hear it when describing rings, necklaces, earrings, watches, or decorative items made with sapphire.
Can be used on its own or before another noun in compounds and descriptions. In everyday speech, it sounds natural in both neutral and formal settings.
For learners, the key point is that it refers to the stone itself, not the colour blue in general. If you want to talk about blue colour, use a different word.
